# 1 Maccabees Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_015_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Antiochus, son of the late King Demetrius, was somewhere out in the islands when he sent a letter to Simon the priest and ethnarch of the Jews and to the entire Jewish nation.

**2** It read: "King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and ethnarch and to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**3** Traitors have seized our ancestral kingdom. I intend to reclaim it and restore it to what it was. I have raised a large army and fitted out a fleet.

**4** My plan is to march through the country and take vengeance on those who have devastated it and destroyed cities throughout my kingdom.

**5** I hereby confirm all the tax exemptions granted you by previous kings, along with whatever other privileges they gave you.

**6** I also grant you the right to mint your own currency.

**7** Jerusalem and the sanctuary shall be free. Every weapon you have stockpiled, every stronghold you have built and hold — they are yours.

**8** Whatever debts are owed to the royal treasury, past or future — all of it, from this day forward and forever, I release.

**9** When we have secured the kingdom, we will honor you and your nation and the temple with magnificent honors, and your fame will spread throughout the world."

**10** In 138 BCE, Antiochus landed in his ancestral territory. The armies flocked to him — leaving Trypho with almost no one.

**11** Antiochus drove him north; Trypho fled to the coastal city of Dor.

**12** He had no choice — his situation was desperate and his army had abandoned him.

**13** Antiochus pitched camp before Dor with a hundred and twenty thousand infantry and eight thousand cavalry.

**14** He ringed the city, brought the fleet in from the sea, and threw a combined land-and-sea blockade around it — nothing in, nothing out.

**15** Around this time, Numenius and his delegation returned from Rome carrying official letters addressed to various kings and territories. They read:

**16** "Lucius, consul of Rome, to King Ptolemy, greetings.

**17** Envoys of the Jews — our friends and allies — have come to us to renew the ancient friendship and alliance, sent by Simon the high priest and the Jewish people.

**18** They brought a gold shield worth a thousand minas.

**19** We have therefore decided to write to the various kings and countries: do not attack the Jews, do not make war against them, their cities, or their land, and do not support anyone who fights against them.

**20** We have accepted the shield they brought.

**21** If any traitors from Judea have fled to your territory, hand them over to Simon the high priest to be dealt with under their own law."

**22** Identical letters went to Demetrius, Attalus, Ariarathes, and Arsaces,

**23** and to all the territories: Sampsames, Sparta, Delos, Myndos, Sicyon, Caria, Samos, Pamphylia, Lycia, Halicarnassus, Cos, Side, Aradus, Rhodes, Phaselis, Gortyna, Cnidus, Cyprus, and Cyrene.

**24** A copy was sent to Simon the high priest.

**25** Antiochus kept hammering at Dor — assault after assault, siege engines and all — keeping Trypho completely sealed in.

**26** Simon sent Antiochus two thousand elite troops, along with silver, gold, and large quantities of supplies.

**27** Antiochus refused everything. He threw out all the previous agreements with Simon and cut him off completely.

**28** He sent his friend Athenobius to deliver an ultimatum: "You are holding Joppa, Gazara, and the Jerusalem citadel — all cities of my kingdom.

**29** You have ravaged the surrounding regions, caused tremendous harm to the country, and seized dozens of locations that belong to my kingdom.

**30** Either hand over the cities you have taken and pay tribute on all the territory you have occupied beyond Judea's borders,

**31** or pay a thousand talents of silver as compensation — five hundred for the destruction and five hundred in back tribute. Otherwise we march."

**32** Athenobius came to Jerusalem and was stopped in his tracks by what he saw: Simon's court in all its splendor — a sideboard loaded with gold and silver vessels, and an impressive entourage. He was stunned. He delivered the king's message.

**33** Simon replied calmly: "We have not taken foreign land. We have not seized what belongs to others. We took back our ancestral inheritance — the land our enemies had held unjustly for a time.

**34** When the opportunity came, we reclaimed what was always ours.

**35** As for Joppa and Gazara — those cities were actively harmful to our people and our land. We'll pay you a hundred talents for them."

**36** Athenobius said nothing. He walked out in a fury, went back to the king, and gave him a full report — including a vivid account of Simon's wealth and splendor. The king erupted in rage.

**37** Trypho slipped out to sea and escaped to Orthosia.

**38** Antiochus appointed a general named Cendebaeus as governor of the coastal region, giving him infantry and cavalry.

**39** His orders: establish a base opposite Judea, fortify Kidron, and wage war against the people. Antiochus himself continued hunting Trypho.

**40** Cendebaeus moved to Jamnia and began a campaign of provocation — raiding Judea, killing and kidnapping civilians.

**41** He fortified Kidron and based cavalry and infantry there to raid the roads of Judea, exactly as the king had directed.
